topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: It introduces the final lecture of the course and outlines the key learning objectives for understanding cancer therapies.

topics.label: Local interventions, cytotoxic chemotherapy, and drug resistance
topics.groupedBecause: They describe conventional cancer treatment modalities—surgery, radiotherapy, and cytotoxic chemotherapy—along with their associated systemic toxicities and efflux-mediated resistance.

topics.label: Targeting intrinsic cellular vulnerabilities and DNA repair defects
topics.groupedBecause: They examine therapeutic strategies that exploit intrinsic cancer vulnerabilities, including hormone dependence, cell cycle checkpoint deficiencies, and defective DNA repair pathways.

topics.label: Oncogenic kinase targeting and mechanisms of resistance
topics.groupedBecause: They explain the development and mechanism of small-molecule inhibitors directed against driver kinases and detail the structural and pathway-level adaptations that lead to drug resistance.

topics.label: Monoclonal antibody therapies and antibody-drug conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: They discuss the therapeutic use of engineered monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates to target cell surface antigens on cancer cells.

topics.label: Cancer immune surveillance and immunotherapy
topics.groupedBecause: They evaluate the evidence for immune surveillance against tumors and outline therapeutic strategies designed to reactivate and direct T-cell responses against cancer.

topics.label: Current challenges, historical progress, and future perspectives in cancer care
topics.groupedBecause: They reflect on historical trends in cancer survival and prevention, review persistent challenges such as tumor heterogeneity, and consider future clinical and ethical paradigms in cancer management.
